newsitem.title: ITALY: Officials hold talks on debt pact implementation.
newsitem.headline: Officials hold talks on debt pact implementation.

text.p: Officials from creditor nations were meeting in Paris on Thursday to start implementing an agreement to provide relief for countries suffering from the worst debt, World Bank president James Wolfensohn said.

The meeting aims to draw up the first countries to benefit from the deal -- reached last Septmeber -- in which the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Paris Club of creditor states all plan to improve their help for the most indebted nations, he told reporters.
"In Paris today we will probably be nominating the countries we start with," Wolfensohn told a briefing on the margins of a U.N.-sponsored food summit.
Wolfenson told Reuters it was not yet clear which countries would be the first receive help, adding the meeting was not being held under the auspices of the Paris Club.
A World Bank official said the talks grouped experts from the World Bank, IMF, multilateral banks and creditor nations.
Under the initiative, the Paris Club of creditor nations will improve debt relief to the world's poorest nations while the World Bank and IMF will also provide additional funds.
The Paris Club has refused to say which countries are likely to benefit from the new terms of debt relief.
